A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, despite the title change and FedAID-to-FedDRA rename. All 25 pages of v2 and 24 pages of v3, including appendices, figures, tables, equations, and rasterized pseudocode, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original federated pre-training experiments, downstream classification, segmentation and retrieval results, and appendix ablations and diagnostic analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original chest X-ray experiments and analyses, plus retinal pre-training and downstream diabetic-retinopathy and edema-risk classification results.

M1.justification: v2 alternates guided whole-model training with learning a robust teacher alignment module using the separate Ldro objective. v3 trains alignment modules with frozen encoders before joint training, uses frozen global-model representations as anchors, and applies DRO client weighting and the same constrained objective in both stages. Sections 4 and Algorithms 1–3 therefore describe substantive procedural and objective changes beyond renaming.

E1.justification: v3 adds retinal pre-training on MESSIDOR and BRSET and diabetic-retinopathy and edema-risk evaluation on portable-device MBRSET data. It removes v2's EHRXQA-based out-of-distribution retrieval evaluation. MIMIC-CXR retrieval and RSNA/Covidx downstream coverage remain; relabeling retrieval as in-domain does not itself introduce another dataset.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 adds FedX and FedU comparisons with GLoRIA and FedLDAWA with MGCA. The chest X-ray comparison drops v2 Table 1's FedMAE and ImageNet-initialized baseline rows, although FedMAE participates in the new retinal experiment. Centralized and decentralized comparisons remain in v3's appendix.

E3.justification: The reported MIMIC-CXR batch size changes from 388 to 288–388 and the main uncertainty radius from 1 to 0.1; disease-label sourcing changes from ChestImaGenome to MIMIC-CXR. v3 adds an LDA heterogeneity setting of 5 and a retinal protocol using batch size 100, 20 communication rounds, and 10%/20%/100% downstream training fractions. These are reported setting changes, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2's teacher-averaging and L2-versus-contrastive-guidance ablations are replaced by removals of two-stage training, global constraints, and DRO weighting in v3 Table 3. v3 adds heterogeneity sensitivity and client-similarity training dynamics. The earlier distortion matrices and downstream-performance convergence sweep are removed; several motivating client-retraining analyses are retained and relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard errors, or significance tests. Cross-client averages, worst-client performance, and disparity describe heterogeneity rather than run-to-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: New retinal, baseline, heterogeneity, and ablation results are added, while EHRXQA and several earlier diagnostic results are removed. Between v2 Table 1 and v3 Table 2, the proposed ConVIRT method's recall@1 changes from 29.49 to 30.2 and its 1% Covidx accuracy from 82.50 to 81.0. These accompany revised methods/settings and are not controlled same-setting gains; many retained appendix diagnostics merely undergo rounding.

T1.justification: v2's Remark 1 and Appendix G provide Lipschitz-based guidance and alignment arguments. v3 replaces these with Proposition 1 and Appendix D's InfoNCE lemma and target-risk derivation involving local/global encoder discrepancies. The new proof introduces a target distribution expressed as a mixture of client distributions, changing the formal claims, assumptions, and derivation.

C1.justification: The overarching goal of robust federated medical VLP remains, but the central contribution is redefined. v2 emphasizes binding local representations to a learned unbiased teacher alignment; v3's abstract and introduction emphasize optimization over potential downstream-domain distributions through globally constrained, two-stage training.

C2.justification: v3 interprets DRO through client step-size allocation and bridging pre-training/downstream domain gaps. Its larger-radius OOD-transfer versus in-domain-retrieval tradeoff replaces the small-radius recommendation supported by v2 Table 7 and Figure 11, although v2's prose was internally inconsistent. v3 also omits Appendix H's explicit caveats about parameter-based privacy leakage and scarce paired data for complex medical modalities.

D1.justification: v3 adds the retinal caption template, associated training hyperparameters, and A100 hardware as an alternative to A40. It removes v2's detailed client-disease allocation tables, explicit 224×224 resizing instruction, and 500-step retraining details. Much of the backbone and existing implementation documentation remains.

R1.justification: The positioning shifts toward mutual-information alignment, global constraints, and last-layer guidance, adding discussion of Su et al. (2023), Legate et al. (2024), FedX, FedU, and L-DAWA. Earlier FedDAT/ZooPFL and other federated multimodal discussions are removed. The comparison matrix is substantively rewritten from v2 Table 18 to v3 Table 1, including new technical comparison criteria.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, problem formulation, method explanation, and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten. Empirical findings move into an expanded main-text discussion, experiment settings gain domain-specific subsections, and appendices A–H are reorganized into A–D. The title, method name, and author information also change.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redesigned, and v2 Figures 5, 6, and 8 are combined into v3 Figure 3. Main results tables are reorganized, centralized/decentralized results move to the appendix, and retinal and heterogeneity tables are added. Analysis plots are replaced or consolidated, pseudocode is retypeset, and the document adopts the TMLR layout.

improvement.justification: v3 adds valuable institutional retinal validation, relevant comparators, and component-removal ablations. However, it removes privacy caveats and allocation details, while its new consistent-robustness claim conflicts with Table 5: for GLoRIA at heterogeneity 1, RSNA 1% accuracy is 81.8 for FedDRA versus 83.2 for FedAvg. Appendix D also assumes a client-mixture target distribution, leaving support for the broader OOD framing unclear. These benefits and losses in rigor and transparency prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
